eligibility.quote: If two or more transforms are sended from the same node using successive calls to: tf2_ros.TransformBroadcaster().sendTransform() ... only the last one is received by the tf core.

failed_conditions.quote:
It looks like the c++ broadcaster as [a sending queue of 100](https://github.com/ros/geometry_experimental/blob/indigo-devel/tf2_ros/src/transform_broadcaster.cpp#L42)
while the python implementation has [a send queue of 1](https://github.com/ros/geometry_experimental/blob/indigo-devel/tf2_ros/src/tf2_ros/transform_broadcaster.py#L44)

loudness.quote: only the last one is received by the tf core. If a delay is introduced by successive calls, all the transformations are received.

resolution.quote:
-        self.pub_tf = rospy.Publisher("/tf", TFMessage, queue_size=1)
+        self.pub_tf = rospy.Publisher("/tf", TFMessage, queue_size=100)

notes: Eligibility agreed (stop_step 6, PAIR, topic /tf). Issue #89 body carries the Python reproducer and 'only the last one is received by the tf core'; tfoote's comment 83259331 names the queue mismatch (100 in C++ vs 1 in Python). PR #90 changes queue_size=1 to queue_size=100, matching the spec's resolution summary. FAILED-CONDITION CLASS ERROR: the class field reads 'qos_reliability', but the defect is the rospy publisher's outgoing message-queue depth (queue_size=1 drops all but the newest message when several are enqueued before the publishing thread sends), which is not a reliability QoS policy (and ROS 1 has no such policy). The spec's own notes state 'it is recorded as other'. Correct class is 'other' (rate_shortfall is the nearest named alternative). Elements topic:/tf agreed. Loudness silent/run agreed (message loss with no ROS diagnostic). Resolution 'recommended' agreed (fix merged; reporter re-run not shown).
